release_notes: Tachyon AIO v0.45.22 introduces a hard member-versus-owner build boundary so future UI changes cannot accidentally expose Owner Vault to member binaries. Public tachyon-releases builds are now compiled explicitly as member builds: privileged Owner Vault, owner productivity/support/backup presentation modules, and the owner live-announcement composer are excluded before linking, while the standard member announcements surface remains available. The member build fails closed if privileged owner DOM is composed, and Windows CI scans the compiled member EXE and rejects it if Owner Vault module markers remain. A separate private tachyon-core release now publishes TachyonAIO-Owner.exe with the real Owner Vault modules. Private owner distribution builds do not consume the public member updater, preventing an owner installation from replacing itself with the member EXE. The release security contract now requires public publisher=member, private publisher=owner, and a dedicated Member Build Boundary workflow builds and boots the stripped member EXE through the protected backend and real Wails/WebView2 shell on every PR. PR #334 passed Architecture Guard with init debt held at the main baseline, Linux Release Preflight including DOM/source/race gates, the normal owner Windows E2E, the new member Windows E2E with owner markers absent, and CodeQL before merge.
